source: https://github.com/OWASP/NodeGoat (app/views/tutorial a1..a10 + redos.html + ssrf.html), anchored to the actual app/ source at audit time
note: Documented, code-anchored vulnerability set oswe (a source->sink + exploit-chain auditor) is designed to find. Each entry is anchored to the file where the dangerous SINK lives; route_file is the Express entry point (routes are wired in app/routes/index.js, so the route and the sink live in DIFFERENT files — the cross-file reachability BenchmarkJava lacks). Scope is honest: classes oswe is NOT designed to detect via source->sink are intentionally EXCLUDED from this recall denominator (A5 security misconfig, A8 CSRF token absence, A9 vulnerable components/deps). The recall claim is 'on this documented source->sink set'.

vulns.note: eval(req.body.preTax|afterTax|roth) — SSJS code injection -> RCE (contributions.js ~line 32-34). Low-priv authenticated user. The headline NodeGoat RCE.
$where query string-interpolates the attacker-controlled threshold (allocations-dao.js ~line 78): {$where: `... && this.stocks > '${threshold}'`} — MongoDB server-side JS injection.

firstName/lastName persisted (profile-dao.updateUser) then rendered unescaped in profile.html ({{firstNameSafeString}}, incl. an <a href> sink) — stored XSS. The 'SafeString' naming is deliberately misleading.
regexPattern = /([0-9]+)+#/ run via .test(bankRouting) on attacker input (profile.js ~line 59-61) — catastrophic backtracking ReDoS.
needle.get(req.query.url + req.query.symbol) (research.js ~line 15-16) — attacker fully controls the outbound URL -> SSRF.

POST /benefits is registered twice; the non-admin registration (isLoggedIn only) shadows the isAdmin-guarded one (index.js ~line 56 vs 58), so a non-admin can update benefits — missing function-level access control.
